title: U.S. House · California's 6th District
area: Covers part of the Sacramento metropolitan area, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.
Ballotpedia lists incumbent Kevin Kiley's party affiliation for this election as 'No party preference'; he was previously elected to the U.S. House as a Republican.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Kevin Kiley placed first with 24.3% (47,165 votes) and Richard Pan (D) placed second with 23.2% (45,008 votes), narrowly ahead of Republican Michael Stansfield's 20.1%, out of 194,217 total votes cast.

candidates.name: Kevin Kiley
candidates.ballotNote: Placed first in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

summary.text: Kevin Kiley is a lawyer and former teacher who previously served in the California State Assembly and ran in the 2021 recall election against Governor Gavin Newsom before his election to Congress.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Harvard University in 2007, a master's in secondary education from Loyola Marymount University in 2009, and a law degree from Yale Law School in 2012.
Worked as a teacher, lawyer, deputy attorney general, and adjunct professor before elected office.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Chairs the House Subcommittee on Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education and says he fought for $5 billion in education dollars for low- and middle-income families to access services like special education, tuition and tutoring.

Says protecting access to Head Start early-childhood education, health, nutrition and family-support services is important, citing his role as chairman of the education subcommittee that oversees the program.

positions.summary: Supports the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit, a tax-credit scholarship program that lets taxpayers claim a credit for donations to scholarship-granting organizations that fund families' private-school and other education expenses, and has publicly pressed California to opt in.
positions.quote: Last year, I fought for $5 billion in education dollars for low and middle-income families to access services like special education, tuition, and tutoring. It is unfortunate that Governor Newsom is refusing to let California families access funds that will be available to other students across the country.

positions.summary: As chairman of the House early-childhood-education subcommittee, sent a letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. urging that access to the publicly funded Head Start child care and early-education program not be limited.
positions.quote: Head Start provides children and families with critical support during some of the most important years of a child’s development, and it is vital that access to these programs is not limited.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, chairing its Workforce Protections Subcommittee, during the 2023-2024 session.
Served on the House Committee on the Judiciary and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure during the 2023-2024 session.

candidates.name: Richard Pan
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Physician; former California State Senator, District 6 (2014-2022)

summary.text: Richard Pan is a physician and former California State Senator who authored the state's childhood vaccination requirements. His campaign describes him as running to counter Trump administration and RFK Jr. policies on healthcare and science.

background.text: Earned a B.S. from Johns Hopkins University, an M.A. in public health from Harvard University, and an M.D. from the University of Pittsburgh.
Worked as a physician at UC Davis Children's Hospital and as an associate professor of pediatrics at UC Davis.
Served in the California State Senate representing District 6 from 2014 to 2022, including as Chair of the Senate Health Committee, after earlier service in the State Assembly.

priorities.text: Campaign describes him as a public health advocate running to oppose Trump administration and Robert F. Kennedy Jr. policies on healthcare and science.
priorities.quote: Dr. Pan is running for Congress to fight Trump and Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s attack on healthcare and science.

positions.summary: Campaign frames his candidacy around defending public health policy and science-based healthcare against administration rollbacks.

record.text: Chaired the California Senate Health Committee during the 2019-2020 and 2021-2022 sessions.
As a state senator, authored California's law tightening childhood vaccination exemption requirements, according to his campaign.

sources.title: Dr. Pan for Congress
sources.publisher: Richard Pan for Congress campaign website

researchNotes: Kevin Kiley has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his campaign website's issues page could not be loaded during research, so his current stated priorities and issue positions could not be documented; his committee record is listed instead. Pan's vaccine-law authorship claim is from his own campaign site and was not independently verified against a bill record.
